title: ChatScene: Knowledge-Enabled Safety-Critical Scenario Generation for Autonomous Vehicles

control_signal.value: Unstructured natural-language scenario description (human- or LLM-written), split into adversarial behavior, road geometry and relative spawn position.

control_mechanism.value: LLM decomposes text with few-shot prompts; sentence embeddings retrieve matching Scenic code snippets from a database; snippets are assembled into a Scenic program and run in CARLA, with Scenic parameters adversarially optimized.

base_model.value: GPT-4 as the LLM agent, a retrieval database of description-code pairs, Scenic language, CARLA simulator; SAC-trained RL ego vehicles in Safebench.

datasets.value: Safebench with eight CARLA Challenge base scenarios; self-built Scenic snippet database from LLM-generated, manually checked pairs.

metrics.value: Collision rate, overall score (aggregating safety, functionality, etiquette levels), and ADE as scenario diversity measure.

controllability_evidence.value: Generated scenes raise collision rate by 15 % over the strongest baselines; adversarial fine-tuning of ego gives 51 % lower collision rate than original and a further 9 % over SOTA.

notes: Controllability is by text fidelity to executable Scenic code; no direct text-to-code accuracy metric appears in packet, evidence is adversarial strength instead.
